title: Capacity Scenario Garden — Decision Graph & Operator Playbook
author: Leila Moreno
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document is a curated library (the "Capacity Scenario Garden") of concrete capacity failure and surge scenarios observed in the platform, accompanied by a decision graph that maps observable signals to recommended operator actions, dashboard views, and alert responses. The goal is to reduce time-to-resolution and ensure consistent remediation across regions and teams.

Scope: covers multi-tenant GPU pools, regional prefetched KV caches, autoscaler interactions with burst credits, and platform-side routing. This is not a hardware troubleshooting manual (see eng-infra/runbooks).

Summary of deliverables
- Scenario catalog: brief descriptions, root causes, and impact vectors.
- Decision graph: prioritized signals -> recommended remediation path.
- Operator runbooks: step-by-step actions, CLI snippets, and escalation points.
- Dashboards & alert mappings: which panels to open, what to annotate.
- Retrospective checklist: how to capture learnings back into the Garden and roadmap.

Decision principles (high level)
- Safety-first: prefer throttling and fallback to aggressive autoscaler actions over destructive operations.
- Minimize customer-visible regressions: prefer model-variant fallback and region steering before mass reboots.
- Fast experimentability: runbook steps must be reversible and annotated with risk level (low/medium/high).

Decision graph (text form)
1) Detect signal cluster: 
   - Token latency p95 spike > 3x baseline for 5m (platform.telemetry.token_latency_p95)
   - Queue length per-tenant > 200 and backlog growth rate > 10%/min (allocator.queue_length_total)
   - GPU utilization nearing 98% per-pool and sustained (>10m) (gpu_pool.utilization_percent)
   -> Path A: Capacity starvation / hot-tenant surge.

2) Detect signal cluster: 
   - KV cache miss rate > 40% (kv_prefix_cache.miss_rate) + sudden rise in request size
   - Warmup counts < expected for popular prefixes; prefetch hit ratio dropping
   -> Path B: Cold cache or prefetch regression.

3) Detect signal cluster: 
   - Regional network errors between edge and regional-router > 5% (edge_http5xx_total)
   - Model swap / variant fallback rate increases in logs (model_swap.count)
   -> Path C: Network-induced regional degradation.

Each path points to a primary recommended operator playbook below. See Appendix A for the decision graph visual (PNG embedded link placeholder).

Scenario catalog (selected entries)
- Hot-tenant compute storm (Path A)
  - Symptoms: p95 token latency 3–10x, tenant queue ballooning, billing spike alert fired.
  - Typical root causes: runaway background job, misconfigured client retry loop, sudden bot traffic.
  - Immediate impact: increased tail-latency for co-located tenants, risk of eviction cascade.
  - SLOs impacted: global p99 token latency SLO (99.95% target), tenant isolation SLOs.
  - Severity: high.

- Prefetch configuration regression (Path B)
  - Symptoms: KV cache miss-rate up from 6% -> 45%, warm-start failures, increased token cost per request.
  - Typical root causes: deployment that changed prefetch TTLs, quantization-rollout changing prefixes, or regression in prefetch hinting service.
  - Immediate impact: cost increase and latency degradation for previously warm workloads.
  - Severity: medium.

- Regional routing flake (Path C)
  - Symptoms: regional 5xx spike, edge->regional RTT elevated, model swap fallback observed, synthetic lab fails for region.
  - Typical root causes: misconfigured LB, inter-region peering issue, maintenance window overlap.
  - Severity: medium-high.

Operator runbook: Path A — Hot-tenant compute storm (Risk: medium/high)
1) Triage & quick containment (0–5 minutes)
   - Open incident channel and post summary: region, impacted pools, top tenant IDs, relevant alerts.
   - Run quick query to list top 10 tenants by queue growth:
     - CLI: curl -s "https://telemetry.internal/api/query?m=top_tenant_queue_growth&r=5m" | jq '.'
   - If top suspect identified and belongs to non-critical class, apply non-destructive tenant soft-throttle:
     - CLI: POST /platform-allocator/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/soft_throttle {"rate_pct":20}
2) Stabilize capacity (5–20 minutes)
   - If pool GPU utilization > 95%: trigger burst-capacity request to dedicated-burst pool (automated path) or start reserved nodes:
     - CLI: rhctl capacity request --pool gpu-pool-42 --count 4 --reason "hot-tenant surge"
   - If burst request fails or insufficient, shift non-critical tenants to lower-priority pool with lower QoS: rhctl tenant move --from pool-A --to pool-B --selector "priority:low"
3) Remediate root cause (20–90 minutes)
   - If tenant shows runaway API patterns, open support ticket to customer and toggle per-tenant rate-limiting config.
   - If caused by internal job: identify job via job-trace and terminate/rollback.
4) Postmortem & follow-up
   - Tag incident in Garden, add scenario details, and assign an owner to implement a durable guardrail (e.g., autoscale policy tweak or tenant hard-throttle rule).

Operator runbook: Path B — Cold cache/prefetch regression (Risk: low/medium)
1) Verify instrumentation
   - Panels to open: "KV cache hit ratio by prefix", "prefetch success rate", "prefetch latency histogram".
   - Query example: PromQL: rate(kv_prefix_cache_misses_total[5m]) / rate(kv_prefix_cache_requests_total[5m])
2) Quick fixes (5–30 minutes)
   - Roll forward prefetch agent restart in region: k8s rollout restart deploy/prefetch-agent -n platform-region-3
   - If TTL misconfiguration: patch rollout to revert TTL change and bump rollout speed: kubectl apply -f prefetch-config.yaml
   - Re-seed hot prefixes via manual prefetch CLI: rhctl prefetch inject --prefix "marketing-widget" --region eu-west-1 --count 1000
3) Validation
   - Wait 10m and validate kv_prefix_cache.miss_rate drops below 10%.
   - If not resolved, escalate to runtime team (owner: eng-serving-runtime).

Operator runbook: Path C — Regional routing flake (Risk: medium)
1) Immediate routing action (0–10 minutes)
   - Use traffic steering to divert new requests away from affected region:
     - CLI: rhctl routing weight-adjust --route global-edge --region eu-west-1 --weight 0.2
   - Enable fallback to compatible model variant in metadata: POST /model-router/v1/variants/fallback-enable
2) Network diagnostic (10–40 minutes)
   - Check peering and BGP state: opsnetctl bgp status --peer eu-west-1 --verbose
   - Check LB instance health and backend pool drain counters.
3) Restore & gradual reconverge (40–120 minutes)
   - Incrementally restore weights to avoid shock and watch p95.
   - Annotate the incident with timeline and when drain windows occur.

Dashboards & alerts mapping (concrete)
- Root dashboard: "Capacity Scenario Garden — Incident Triage" (Grafana UID: garden-0123) panels:
  - Panel A: Token latency heatmap (timeseries + per-tenant breakdown).
  - Panel B: GPU pool utilization by region (gauge + trend).
  - Panel C: KV prefix hit ratio (stacked bar).
  - Panel D: Tenant queue growth leaderboards.

Key alert rules (examples)
- Alert: capacity:hot_tenant_latency_burst
  - Expr: increase(platform_telemetry_token_latency_p95[5m]) > 3
  - Severity: P0
  - Runbook: follow Path A containment steps.

- Alert: platform:kv_prefetch_miss_regression
  - Expr: kv_prefix_cache_miss_rate > 0.40 for 10m
  - Severity: P2
  - Runbook: follow Path B.

- Alert: platform:region_edge_5xx_surge
  - Expr: sum(rate(edge_http5xx_total[2m])) by (region) / sum(rate(edge_request_total[2m])) by (region) > 0.05
  - Severity: P1
  - Runbook: follow Path C.

Retrospective checklist (to push learnings back into the Garden)
1) Within 48h: create incident stub in Garden with timeline, owner, and initial impact.
2) Within 7 days: produce a short analysis answering: was the decision graph path correct? where were detection gaps?
3) Action items: label by priority and assign owners; add instrumentation tasks to backlog if missing.
4) Add a single-sentence runbook improvement that is stored as a Garden tip and surfaced in the triage dashboard.

Roadmap & next steps
- Q2 2025: Integrate Garden decision graph into the triage chat-bot so on-call can receive recommended remediation steps with one command. Owner: eng-platform.
- Q3 2025: Add synthetic degradations for the top-10 Garden scenarios to the degradation lab (owner: platform-lab).
- Q4 2025: Export standardized JSON incident templates for downstream postmortem tooling.

Ownership and maintenance cadence
- Primary owner: eng-platform — capacity-paths subteam.
- Runbook review cadence: quarterly.
- After any incident classified as Severity=high: owner must update Garden within 7 days.

Appendix A: Example Prometheus alert rule (YAML snippet)

groups:
- name: platform-capacity.rules
  rules:
  - alert: Capacity_HotTenantLatencyBurst
    expr: increase(platform_telemetry_token_latency_p95[5m]) > 3
    for: 2m
    labels:
      severity: P0
    annotations:
      summary: "Token p95 increased more than 3x in 5m for {{ $labels.region }}"

Appendix B: Example escalation contact list
- oncall-platform: paged via PagerDuty (schedule: platform-oncall)
- eng-serving-runtime lead: Marcus Liu (marcus@redwood.example.com)
- platform-allocator owner: Sophe K. (sophie.k@redwood.example.com)

Notes and references
- Related playbooks: predictive-scale-and-eviction-playbook, prefetch-reliability-telemetry-fusion-actionbook.
- Visual decision graph: [Capacity Scenario Garden decision graph — diagram.png] (attach to this page).

How to contribute
- Filing a new scenario: copy the "scenario-template" (link in the page sidebar), fill in symptoms, signals, short remediation, and owner. Add labels: severity and surface area.
- Quick edits: small fixes can be made by Platform engineers and approved by the capacity-paths subteam. Major changes require reviewer sign-off.

Change log
- 2024-11-03: Created by Leila Moreno (initial catalog of 12 scenarios).
- 2025-02-18: Updated decision thresholds for kv_prefix_cache and added Alert rule examples.

End of document
